candidates.next_evidence: Track Eaton quarterly Electrical Americas backlog, data-center orders, capacity expansion commentary, segment margins, book-to-bill, and lead-time commentary.
candidates.node_relation: Reference leader for electrical power distribution equipment, Electrical Americas backlog, data-center electrical orders and broader electrification demand.
candidates.theme_relation: Used to define the demand signal and pricing/backlog context for switchgear, power distribution, grid and data-center electrical infrastructure.
candidates.why_include: Eaton's 2026 Q1 materials reported record Electrical Americas sales and backlog growth, with data-center momentum explicitly cited. This makes ETN the category anchor for validating whether electrical hardware is a real chokepoint rather than a narrative-only theme.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as the reference lane because its scale, coverage and data-center power narrative are already widely recognized.

candidates.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-Q and earnings call for backlog by market, book-to-bill, data-center order concentration, lead times, gross margin durability, capacity additions and customer concentration.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Custom-engineered electrical power distribution and control equipment
candidates.theme_relation: A purer public-market exposure to switchgear, substation, bus duct and electrical balance-of-system capacity than most diversified industrials.

candidates.why_underfollowed: Despite the stock's increased attention, the company is still often classified as a niche industrial electrical manufacturer rather than as a core grid/data-center power bottleneck supplier.

candidates.why_include: PLPC is not a transformer or switchgear OEM, but it supplies the less glamorous hardware layer that supports and connects utility transmission, distribution and substation systems. That makes it a Serenity-style one-step-away candidate for the same grid bottleneck theme.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It has a messy industrial label, small-cap profile, low social/analyst mindshare, family/legacy manufacturer characteristics, and is less obvious than Eaton, GE Vernova, Hubbell or Quanta.

memory_update.text: POWL should remain a high-priority underfollowed/direct candidate for grid electrical hardware because its product list maps unusually cleanly to switchgear, substations, e-houses, bus duct and medium-voltage equipment.

PLPC is a lower-attention small-cap second-order candidate for grid electrical hardware, especially transmission, distribution and substation fittings; it needs deeper verification of Energy segment acceleration and utility capex linkage.
ETN remains the reference leader for backlog/order validation, but its mega-cap status means it should be used mainly as a pricing and demand signal rather than crowding out smaller suppliers.

Need a later pass for transformer-specific public exposure, including non-US ADRs/OTC names, transformer components, specialty steel/copper inputs, insulation fluids, testing/certification and utility substation automation suppliers.

node: Large transformers, switchgear, breakers, busway, substations, and electrical balance-of-system
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the grid electrical hardware node with a two-lane funnel: Eaton as the high-attention reference leader that validates the demand/backlog signal, Powell Industries as a direct but less mega-cap switchgear/substation/e-house exposure, and Preformed Line Products as a small-cap, lower-attention second-order grid hardware supplier tied to transmission, distribution and substation fittings. This pass avoids hyperscaler and generation names and focuses on physical electrical equipment required before new data-center, utility, renewable, industrial or electrification load can interconnect reliably.
